chunks: ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام.
About a man who slaughtered a sheep, and it convulsed and fell into a well of water while its veins were gushing blood: may wudu (ablution) be performed from that well?
He said: "Between thirty and forty buckets should be drawn from it, then wudu (ablution) may be performed from it."
ai.seo_question: If a slaughtered animal falls into a well while still bleeding, can wudu be performed from that water?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about a well into which a slaughtered sheep fell while blood was still flowing from it. The ruling is that a specified amount of water, between thirty and forty buckets, should be drawn from the well before it is used for wudu (ablution).
